The Applicant is seeking anticipatory bail in connection  with C.R.No.68/2024, dated 16/01/2024, registered with  Vakola Police Station, Mumbai, under sections 406, 420 of the  Indian Penal Code.
 6.

Heard Mr. Anand Pande, learned counsel for the  Applicant and Mr. Avinash A. Naik, learned APP for the State.
 7.
The FIR is lodged by one Sanjivani Mhaprolkar.
She  has stated that in 2016 she wanted to purchase a room.
Therefore, she responded to an advertisement and met the  Applicant.
From 2017 to 2022 she had paid Rs.3,90,000/- as  agreed, but in spite of that, the Applicant did not hand over  possession of the room which she had booked.

The FIR mentions that 9 other persons who had paid Mohd. Hanif Shaikh @ Mohd. Hanif Mohd. ... vs The State Of Maharashtra on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111826815/
3  different amounts on different occasions were also not given  possession of their rooms.
 9.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the Applicant submitted that  rooms of all these persons are ready.
Even the room of first  informant is ready for possession and the Applicant is willing to  hand over the possession to the first informant.
As far as the  other persons are concerned, they have not made full payment  as per the agreements.
If these persons make payment, he is  willing to hand over possession to them also.
He submitted that  there is no offence made out and, if at all, there is any  grievance, it is a civil dispute.

10. Considering this, the investigating agency will have to  verify this statement by making enquiries with those persons  mentioned in the FIR in respect of the statement made by the  learned counsel for the Applicant in the Court today.
In this view  of the matter, the Applicant can be protected by way of ad-  interim relief till the next date.

The Applicant can be directed to  attend the concerned police station as and when called.
